**Step 1 - Scene:** A small snack of whole cherry or grape tomatoes on a white paper plate. No other foods are visible.

**Step 2 - Vessel:** White paper plate, about 18 cm diameter. Area = 3.14 × (9)² ≈ 254 cm².

**Step 3 - Items:** About 11 small red tomatoes (cherry/grape type), each roughly 2 cm long. No dressing or oil is visible.

**Step 4 - Area:** The tomatoes cover roughly 30% of the plate, which is about 76 cm². They are spread in a loose cluster, not a single layer.

**Step 5 - Volume:** 76 cm² × ~2.2 cm typical pile height ≈ 167 ml gross volume.

**Step 6 - Grams:** Cut or whole fruit pieces have a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml. 167 ml × 0.6 ≈ 100 g. A per-fruit check gives about 11 tomatoes × ~8 g ≈ 90 g, so I use about 95 g.

**Step 7 - Energy:** Cherry tomatoes are about 18 kcal per 100 g. 95 g × 0.18 ≈ 17 kcal.

**Step 8 - Sanity check:** Eleven small tomatoes at about 95 g and about 17 kcal is plausible for a small, partly covered paper plate. This is a light snack, not a full meal.

**Total:** about 95 g, about 17 kcal.
